The figure version (`euclidean_all`) is rebuilt after them. ### Diagnostics: why are most distances > 0.9? The heatmap above uses the **chord distance**: `decostand(method = "normalize")` scales each sample to length 1, and the Euclidean distance between length-1 vectors runs from 0 (identical) to √2 ≈ 1.41 (no shared features) (Legendre & Gallagher 2001, Oecologia 129:271-280). Values near 1 or above can come from three different causes, and the steps below test each one: 1. **Feature definition**: the `ko_PFAMs_GOs` string splits one KO into many features, so samples share few of them. 2. **Dominance**: on raw TPM, a handful of very highly expressed transcripts make up most of each sample's length. 3. **The transform itself**: compared on the same KO table, do `normalize`, `hellinger` and `rclr` (the transform 04-07 use; Gloor et al. 2017, Front Microbiol 8:2224) separate samples differently? Positive control throughout: three units are true biological replicates with two libraries each (`Von Damm_Vent_Ravelin2`, `Piccard_Vent_Lotsoshrimp`, `Gorda Ridge_Non-vent_Plume`). A distance worth using puts those pairs among the closest pairs. #### Step 0. Helper functions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Sparsity of a raw abundance matrix (rows = samples, cols = features) feature_sparsity <- function(mat) { pres <- mat > 0 shared <- tcrossprod(pres) # features shared by each sample pair tibble(n_samples = nrow(pres), n_features = ncol(pres), prop_zero = mean(!pres), # share of empty cells prop_in_one_sample = mean(colSums(pres) == 1), median_shared = median(shared[upper.tri(shared)])) } # Share of each sample's squared length that comes from its 10 largest features. # This is how much of the chord distance those 10 features control. top10_share <- function(mat) { apply(mat, 1, \(x) { x2 <- sort(x^2, decreasing = TRUE) sum(head(x2, 10)) / sum(x2) }) } # Distance object -> one row per unique sample pair, flagged if the pair is a replicate pair dist_pairs <- function(d) { m <- as.matrix(d) unit <- set_names(str_remove(rownames(m), "\\|.*"), rownames(m)) # sample_id = raw_label|LIB|SAMPLEID as.data.frame(as.table(m)) |> as_tibble() |> rename(a = Var1, b = Var2, dist = Freq) |> mutate(across(c(a, b), as.character)) |> filter(a < b) |> # unique pairs, drop the diagonal mutate(pct = percent_rank(dist), # 0 = closest pair, 1 = farthest replicate_pair = unit[a] == unit[b]) } # Spread and replicate control for one distance dist_diagnostics <- function(d) { dist_pairs(d) |> summarise(n_pairs = n(), min = min(dist), median = median(dist), max = max(dist), cv = sd(dist) / mean(dist), # higher = more contrast between pairs replicate_pct = median(pct[replicate_pair])) # low = replicates among the closest pairs } ``` ::: #### Step 1. Feature definition: `ko_PFAMs_GOs` string vs. KO Builds the same KO table 04-07 use (`paired_L4.RData`, written at the end of 02), one row per library, under the three transforms. Only the transform changes between the three. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} paired_ko <- load_paired(fields = c("Gorda Ridge", "Von Damm", "Piccard"), depth = 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` [load_paired] data/processed/paired_L4.RData (built 2026-10-23 09:06; 318,911 rows) ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ko_mats <- c("normalize", "hellinger", "rclr") |> set_names() |> map(\(tf) build_matrix(paired_ko, "ko_id", min_tpm = 0, transform = tf)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bind_rows(ko_pfam_go = feature_sparsity(t(wide_frenemies_ortholog)), ko = feature_sparsity(ko_mats$rclr$mat), .id = "feature") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: Read: if `prop_in_one_sample` and `prop_zero` are much higher (and `median_shared` much lower) for `ko_pfam_go` than for `ko`, the high distances partly reflect how features are named, not what the communities express. (`n_samples` differs because the `ko_pfam_go` matrix has one column per biological unit: `SAMPLE_NAME_ORDER` is built from `raw_label`, so replicate libraries are summed. The `ko` matrix has one row per library. Summing replicates fills in zeros, so if anything this understates how much sparser `ko_pfam_go` is.) #### Step 2. Dominance by the top transcripts ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bind_rows(ko_pfam_go = enframe(top10_share(t(wide_frenemies_ortholog)), "sample", "top10"), ko = enframe(top10_share(ko_mats$rclr$mat), "sample", "top10"), .id = "feature") |> group_by(feature) |> summarise(min = min(top10), median = median(top10), max = max(top10)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: Read: a median above ~0.5 means fewer than 10 features set more than half of each sample's position, so the chord distance mostly compares those few. `hellinger` (square root) and `rclr` (log) both reduce this. #### Step 3. Spread and replicate control per transform ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} dist_check <- map(ko_mats, "dist") |> map(dist_diagnostics) |> list_rbind(names_to = "transform") dist_check ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} map(ko_mats, "dist") |> map(dist_pairs) |> list_rbind(names_to = "transform") |> mutate(transform = factor(transform, levels = c("normalize", "hellinger", "rclr"))) |> ggplot(aes(x = dist)) + geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey75") + geom_vline(data = \(df) filter(df, replicate_pair), aes(xintercept = dist), colour = "#b74a70", linewidth = 0.8) + facet_wrap(~ transform, scales = "free") + theme_classic() + labs(x = "pairwise distance between libraries", y = "sample pairs", caption = "Pink lines: biological-replicate pairs.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_metat-data-overview_files/figure-html/diag-spread-plot-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: Read: `cv` says how much contrast the distance has (a narrow pile against the ceiling = low cv). `replicate_pct` is where replicate pairs fall among all pairs: near 0 means the distance recognises replicates as most similar, near 0.5 means it cannot tell them from random pairs. In the histogram, pink lines should sit at the far left. #### Step 3b. Is the rclr distance tracking KO richness? In rclr, zeros stay 0, so a KO detected in one library and absent from another adds to their distance. Libraries that detect more KOs can end up far from the rest for that reason alone. Check whether each library's mean distance tracks the number of KOs it detects, and whether the prevalence filter 04 uses (`prevalence_filter(..., 4)`: a KO must be detected in at least 4 libraries) removes the dependence. Richness can also differ between habitats for real reasons, so the last chunk asks whether KO richness differs between vent and non-vent libraries. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} richness_check <- function(m) { dist_pairs(m$dist) |> pivot_longer(c(a, b), values_to = "sample_id") |> group_by(sample_id) |> summarise(mean_dist = mean(dist)) |> left_join(enframe(rowSums(m$mat > 0), "sample_id", "n_kos"), by = "sample_id") } # Same build as 04: KO must be detected in >= 4 libraries ko_mats_prev <- c("normalize", "hellinger", "rclr") |> set_names() |> map(\(tf) build_matrix(prevalence_filter(paired_ko, "ko_id", min_samples = 4), "ko_id", min_tpm = 0, transform = tf)) list(unfiltered = ko_mats$rclr, prevalence_4 = ko_mats_prev$rclr) |> map(richness_check) |> map(\(df) cor.test(~ mean_dist + n_kos, data = df, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)) |> map(\(ct) tibble(rho = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value)) |> list_rbind(names_to = "kos_used") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Spread and replicate control after the prevalence filter map(ko_mats_prev, "dist") |> map(dist_diagnostics) |> list_rbind(names_to = "transform") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} richness_check(ko_mats$rclr) |> left_join(distinct(paired_ko, sample_id, vent_bin), by = "sample_id") |> ggplot(aes(x = n_kos, y = mean_dist, colour = vent_bin)) + geom_point(size = 2.5) + scale_colour_manual(values = c(Vent = "#b74a70", `Non-vent` = "#346D6E"), name = NULL) + theme_classic() + labs(x = "KOs detected in the library", y = "mean rclr distance to other libraries") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_metat-data-overview_files/figure-html/diag-richness-habitat-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Read: if rho drops well below ~0.4 after the filter and `replicate_pct` stays low, the filtered rclr distance is the one to use (and matches 04). If vent and non-vent libraries form separate clouds along the x-axis, part of the richness signal is habitat, not an artifact. #### Step 4. Do the transforms agree? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mantel(ko_mats$hellinger$dist, ko_mats$rclr$dist, method = "spearman", permutations = 999) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Mantel statistic based on Spearman's rank correlation rho Call: mantel(xdis = ko_mats$hellinger$dist, ydis = ko_mats$rclr$dist, method = "spearman", permutations = 999) Mantel statistic r: -0.6111 Significance: 1 Upper quantiles of permutations (null model): 90% 95% 97.5% 99% 0.268 0.326 0.386 0.444 Permutation: free Number of permutations: 999 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} mantel(ko_mats$normalize$dist, ko_mats$rclr$dist, method = "spearman", permutations = 999) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Mantel statistic based on Spearman's rank correlation rho Call: mantel(xdis = ko_mats$normalize$dist, ydis = ko_mats$rclr$dist, method = "spearman", permutations = 999) Mantel statistic r: -0.5671 Significance: 1 Upper quantiles of permutations (null model): 90% 95% 97.5% 99% 0.256 0.341 0.416 0.475 Permutation: free Number of permutations: 999 ``` ::: ::: Read: a high Spearman r (say > 0.8) means the transforms rank sample pairs the same way, so the choice changes the scale, not the conclusion; use `rclr` to match 04-07. A low r means the conclusion depends on the transform and needs to be reported as such. ### Figure: robust Aitchison distance between sample units The distance used in the figures, chosen from the diagnostics above: KOs from the shared analysis set (the same table as 04-07), a KO kept if detected in at least 4 libraries (`prevalence_filter(..., 4)`, as in 04), replicate libraries averaged to their biological unit, then rclr and Euclidean distance (robust Aitchison; Martino et al. 2019, mSystems 4:e00016-19). rclr was the only transform that placed true replicate libraries among the closest pairs (Step 3). It has no fixed maximum, so the colour scale runs over the observed range of each matrix, and the two heatmaps (all units, vent only) are not on the same scale. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Heatmap of a unit x unit distance; the diagonal (0) is left blank plot_unit_distance <- function(d, title = NULL) { m <- as.matrix(d) as.data.frame(as.table(m)) |> as_tibble() |> rename(X = Var1, Y = Var2, VALUE = Freq) |> mutate(across(c(X, Y), as.character)) |> filter(X != Y) |> mutate(PLOT_X_ORDER = factor(X, levels = order_sample_names, labels = label_sample_names), PLOT_Y_ORDER = factor(Y, levels = order_sample_names, labels = label_sample_names)) |> ggplot(aes(x = PLOT_X_ORDER, y = PLOT_Y_ORDER, fill = VALUE)) + geom_tile(color = "white", lwd = 0.75) + scale_fill_stepsn(colors = orange_heat, n.breaks = 6, limits = range(m[upper.tri(m)])) + scale_x_discrete(position = "top") + coord_equal() + theme_classic() + theme(legend.title = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, color = "black", hjust = 0, size = 12), axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black", size = 12)) + labs(x = "", y = "", title = title) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unit_dist_all <- paired_ko |> prevalence_filter("ko_id", min_samples = 4) |> build_matrix("ko_id", min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform, aggregate = "mean") euclidean_all <- plot_unit_distance(unit_dist_all$dist) euclidean_all ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_metat-data-overview_files/figure-html/unit-distance-all-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: > Pairwise functional dissimilarity across all samples based on KEGG identities. KOs detected in fewer than 4 libraries were removed, and scaled TPM was summed by KO within each library and averaged across replicates. Data were transformed using a robust centered-log-ratio, where non-zero values are log transformed and zeroes remain zero. A euclidean distance was performed on rclrmatrix to form the robust Aitchison distance. ### Vent only Same build restricted to vent libraries. The prevalence filter runs within the vent libraries (as in 04's vent-only models), so the KO set differs from the all-unit matrix. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unit_dist_vent <- paired_ko |> filter(vent_bin == "Vent") |> prevalence_filter("ko_id", min_samples = 4) |> build_matrix("ko_id", min_tpm = 0, transform = params$transform, aggregate = "mean") euclidean_ventonly <- plot_unit_distance(unit_dist_vent$dist, title = "vent only") euclidean_ventonly ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](03_metat-data-overview_files/figure-html/unit-distance-vent-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: #
